perspective:
Harold’s available information:

- He has a friendly/professional relationship with Arthur Begum and has previously relied on Arthur for advice/support.
- **Scenario 1:** Harold feels frustrated and anxious about his project’s progress and believes his team lacks motivation. He arranges and attends a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. He tells Arthur the team seems unmotivated and progress is suffering, and he is at his wit’s end. He hears Arthur suggest understanding each team member’s individual drives and having one-on-one conversations. Harold admits he has focused mainly on goals/deadlines, agrees to try Arthur’s advice, thanks him, and feels more hopeful.
- **Scenario 2:** Harold feels hopeful and relieved after talking with Arthur. He believes Arthur’s advice will help and decides to implement it. He tells his team he wants one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. He says he will schedule time with each and urges them to make the project a success together.
- **Scenario 3:** Harold notices the team still is not responding well after trying the new strategy. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future. He tells Arthur the team still isn’t responding and he is worried. He hears Arthur suggest deeper issues may be involved, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold says he will set up another round of meetings and thanks Arthur.
- **Scenario 4:** Harold feels determined and focused, believing there may be underlying team issues he has not addressed. In one-on-one meetings, he asks team members to share concerns. He hears Team Member 1 report tension among a few team members affecting work. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and asks if there is anything else. He hears Team Member 2 report feeling overwhelmed by workload and stressed. Harold says he understands, will consider redistributing tasks, and says their well-being is important.
- **Scenario 5:** Harold feels optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns will improve team performance. He tells the team he will create a more supportive environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He hears Team Member 1 say it sounds great and will help, and Team Member 2 agree that concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad, urges working together, and says their input and well-being are crucial.

Excluded from Harold’s access: Arthur’s private/internal thoughts, team members’ private feelings beyond what they explicitly said, hidden events, and narrator-only details such as personality typings, degrees, or races unless Harold already knew them.
